name: Treaty with the Creeks, 1805 (first Treaty of Washington)
promises: Article 1: the Creeks ceded the land between the Oconee and Ocmulgee rivers but kept title and possession of a tract five miles long and three wide at the old Ocmulgee fields, where the President could keep a military post and trading house.
Article 2: the United States gained a right to a horse path through Creek country from the Ocmulgee to Mobile, with the Creeks to keep boats and houses of entertainment along it.

Article 3: for the land, the path and the post, the United States would pay twelve thousand dollars a year for eight years and eleven thousand dollars a year for the ten years after, in money, goods or farm implements as the Creeks chose.
Article 4: two blacksmiths and two strikers for eight years.
today: In Docket 292 the Creek Nation claimed that the United States had disbursed only $169,452.25 of the $206,000 owed under Article 3 of this treaty. The Indian Claims Commission dismissed the claim in 1959, holding that the burden of proving the failure lay on the nation. This was a ruling against the nation. The Inter-Tribal Council of the Five Civilized Tribes (Resolution 2002-18) says the treaty excluded the Ocmulgee Old Fields reserve tract from the cession and that Muscogee people were later forced to cede all their Georgia lands through subsequent treaties. The Court of Claims affirmed the Docket 292 dismissal per curiam on March 1, 1961 (152 Ct. Cl. 747), over a dissent that would have put the burden of accounting on the United States, and the Supreme Court affirmed by an equally divided Court (370 U.S. 157), as the Court of Claims report records.

nationVoice.nation: Inter-Tribal Council of the Five Civilized Tribes (of which the Muscogee (Creek) Nation is a member)
nationVoice.summary: The Council says Article 1 of this treaty kept the Ocmulgee Old Fields "Reserve Tract" out of the cession, that the Muscogee were later forced to cede all their Georgia lands, and it affirms the Old Fields as a Muscogee traditional cultural property.

openQuestions: Whether all eighteen annual payments under Article 3 were made is unresolved: the Commission found disbursements definitely allocated to this treaty of $169,452.25 against an admitted obligation of $206,000, but dismissed the claim for want of proof (Docket 292, 1959). No Commission claim for additional payment for the land itself was found.
The Ocmulgee reserve tract kept by Article 1 passed out of Creek hands under a later treaty; that loss belongs to the later treaty's record.
The Muscogee (Creek) Nation's own published account of this treaty was not found in this pass; the Inter-Tribal Council resolution is the closest.

Audit 2026-11-08: the researcher wrote that Docket 292 does not cover this treaty. Its findings of fact quote Article 3 of this treaty and its opinion addresses the claim; today and openQuestions corrected and the two Docket 292 documents added to sources. Status unchanged: the dismissal is a ruling against the nation, not a breach.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for creek, 1805 and 7 Stat. 96; found only the appeal of Docket 292 (152 Ct. Cl. 747, 1961), which affirmed the dismissal, a ruling against the nation added to today. Status unchanged.
